headlines.title: Giants legend Duane Kuiper reveals throat cancer diagnosis, undergoing treatment
headlines.description: SAN FRANCISCO — Kruk and Kuip plan to call their final game together on Sept. 27, but the road to get there won’t be easy. A few weeks after Mike Krukow announced that this will be his final season, Duane Kuiper revealed Sunday that he has been diagnosed with throat cancer. Kuiper is getting treatment and will miss some upcoming games, but he plans to be in the booth next weekend with Krukow for their final series together. “I was recently diagnosed with throat cancer and began treatment last week with my doctors at Stanford Medicine,” Kuiper said in a statement released by the Giants. “This cancer is unrelated to the one I experienced five years ago, and I’m optimistic that it will be successfully treated. I’ll miss the broadcasts tomorrow and Wednesday as I continue treatment, but I’m looking forward to returning Tuesday and this weekend to celebrate my partner, Mike Krukow, and his remarkable career as he calls his final game before retirement. I’m incredibly grateful for the care I’m receiving and for the tremendous support from my family, the Giants organization, my broadcast partners and so many others.” Kuiper, 76, missed this weekend’s series against the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Jon Miller and Dave Flemming filling in. He has long planned to be back next weekend, when he and Krukow, his broadcast partner and closest friend, will call games against the Dodgers for the final time. It will be the end of a 36-year run for Krukow, who announced last month that he is retiring because his long battle with inclusion body myositis has made it difficult to continue to keep up with the physical demands of the job. Kuiper, who underwent chemotherapy in 2021, has said that he intends to keep calling games beyond this season. headlines.title: California establishes Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day under new law
headlines.description: California has officially established Sept. 25 as Dolly Parton Day in honor of the renowned singer, songwriter, philanthropist and actress, the governor’s office announced Sunday. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 931, authored by State Senators Shannon Grove, R-Bakersfield, and John Laird, D-Santa Cruz. The date — 9/25 — was selected as a clever nod to Parton’s beloved hit song “9 to 5,” according to the governor’s office. “We could all afford to live a little more like Dolly. Be kind, be humble, and have some fun… Be a diamond in a rhinestone world,” Newsom said in a statement. “With this bill, we are not just establishing a day to celebrate Dolly Parton, we are creating an annual reminder to us, every year, to live the way she did — joyfully, graciously, and with a whole lot of heart.” Dubbed the “Queen of Country,” Parton is celebrated as one of the most successful country music performers in history, having sold more than 100 million records worldwide. Over her six-decade career, she achieved 25 number-one hits — the most by any female country artist. Her iconic anthem “I Will Always Love You” topped the charts twice, in 1974 and 1982, before Whitney Houston later covered it to enormous global acclaim. Beyond music, Parton built an enduring legacy in acting, producing, and business. Her contributions to Hollywood include her acting debut in the feminist comedy film “9 to 5,” as well as both the 1992 film and the hit television series “Buffy the Vampire Slayer,” for which she served as an uncredited producer. Lawmakers emphasized that Parton’s impact stretches far beyond entertainment, particularly highlighting her humanitarian work and commitment to early childhood literacy through the Imagination Library. The program has distributed more than 300 million books to children worldwide, including across California. “Dolly Parton sparkled on every stage she ever stood on, but her brightest sparkle was the literacy legacy she built through the Imagination Library,” Grove said. “I am incredibly proud of the bipartisan work we have accomplished, from bringing her bilingual reading program statewide in California with former Senate President pro Tempore Toni Atkins, to introducing a bipartisan bill with Senator Laird to establish this annual day of remembrance.” The love Dolly gave so freely, rooted in her deep and openly shared faith, and the love the world returned to her, shows how deeply she was cherished by everyone. I thank Governor Newsom for signing SB 931 so that every September 25th, our state will remember the legend who put millions of books in the hands of our youngest readers and inspired the world on how to respect and love one another,” Grove added. Laird echoed those sentiments, noting Parton’s deep ties to the state. “I’m grateful to Governor Newsom for signing our bill and to Senator Grove for her partnership in making September 25 Dolly Parton Day in California,” Laird said in a statement. “Dolly brought joy to a lot of people, but her legacy goes well beyond her music. Through the Imagination Library, she put books into the hands of millions of children, and throughout her life she led with kindness, acceptance, and a belief that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity and respect. She was also no stranger to the Central Coast, where she performed for packed crowds and spent time over the years. Now, every 9-2-5, California gets to celebrate Dolly and the remarkable legacy she shared with all of us,” Laird said. headlines.title: Baby born in San Francisco traffic after family pulls over for 911 help
headlines.description: A healthy baby girl made an unexpected roadside arrival Friday afternoon after her family got stuck in heavy traffic on the way to the hospital, according to the San Francisco Fire Department. The unexpected delivery began at approximately 4:40 p.m., when crews received a report of a family en route to a hospital to deliver their baby, the department announced Saturday. Fire officials said due to heavy traffic near Crossover Drive and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, the family pulled over and called 911. SFFD Paramedic Engine 14 and AMR Unit 110, a 911 provider for San Francisco, were dispatched to the scene. AMR Unit 110 arrived first, but traffic conditions forced the crew to park two blocks away and run to reach the patient. Personnel arrived just in time to assist with the delivery of the baby girl. Engine 14 crews arrived shortly afterward to provide care for both the mother and the newborn. Both the mother and child were later transported to a local hospital and reported to be in good condition, the department stated. “We want to congratulate the family and welcome this new child to the world,” the SFFD said in a statement. “Her arrival is a true testament to the dedication, compassion and teamwork of our first responders.”

headlines.title: Bay Area students turn old tennis balls into eco-friendly tools
headlines.description: A group of local high school students in the Bay Area is serving the planet by turning old tennis balls into useful community tools. Thousands of used tennis balls are finding a new purpose at schools, animal shelters, and assisted living centers around the Bay Area, courtesy of Bin to Better, a student-led environmental organization that transforms waste into opportunity. Because the rubber and felt on a tennis ball cannot be recycled, about 125 million of them end up in landfills each year. To combat this, members of the Bin to Better organization rally on their time off, sorting through donations collected at local tennis clubs. The students cut the balls open so they can be repurposed as chair leg covers in classrooms, glides on walkers at assisted living homes and enrichment toys for pets. Fremont Elementary teacher Ms. MacKenzie notes that the modified balls work great to keep classrooms quieter while preventing scratches on the floor. The initiative is also making a splash environmentally. Kim Grant, director of the Kim Grant Tennis Academy in Palo Alto, is glad to be part of Bin to Better, saying the effort helps keep nearby waterways clean. As the organization expands and thinks outside the box for community waste solutions, founders encourage community members to ask around at local tennis clubs or check out the Bin to Better website to join the rally.

headlines.title: Alameda County health authorities alert of possible measles exposure
headlines.description: State and Bay Area health officials warned of a possible measles exposure Friday after a person infected with the disease traveled by train from the Midwest through California. Alameda County and California Department of Public health officials say an Amtrak passenger, infected with Measles, traveled from Chicago, through Sacramento, then to Emeryville, before the last leg of their journey to Los Angeles. They said that person could have infected scores of other passengers all along the way. Two frequent riders on the Sacramento to the Bay Area route just heard about the possible measles exposure on Saturday. “That is new news that I’m hearing about. It’s very worrisome,” passenger Elham A said. “It’s a risk you take in any public space. I don’t think Amtrak is particularly at fault for anything related to that. When you use public transport, if people are being silly, it can affect you,” passenger Henry N. said. According to officials, the infected passenger started their trip in Chicago on Sep. 10 and arrived in Los Angeles on Sept. 12. The passenger arrived in Bakersfield and traveled to Stockton that same day. On Sept. 13, the passenger traveled from Oroville to Sacramento, and then from Sacramento to Emeryville. On Sept. 14, the passenger left Emeryville to arrive in Denver on Tuesday. Health experts say measles cases have skyrocketed as vaccination rates have decrease; 3,400 were reported nationwide in 2026, while there were fewer than 2,300 in all of 2025. “So, we have been having the largest Measles outbreak, in since the last 35 years in this country, and now this person riding on Amtrak, actively infected with Measles, could unfortunately infect people who are not vaccinated,” UCSF Department of Medicine Dr. Monica Gandhi said. Dr. Gandhi says vaccination rates for the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine have fallen below the critical 95-percent rate across the U.S., and nine out of 10 patients hospitalized with measles are unvaccinated. “So, we really want 95% rates of vaccination, and the reason Measles is spreading in this country and we’re in this situation, is because we have people who are unvaccinated,” she said. California does still meet the 95% MMR vaccination rate, but a recent Reuters poll says only about 84% of U.S. citizens have faith in vaccines. Gandhi says there’s also a risk with vaccinated people who came into contact with the measles positive Amtrak passenger or others actively infected. She says they can still pick up and carry the disease and transmit it to others. “The concern is, you could take it home to someone who’s vulnerable, who is not vaccinated, like say a small child,” she said. The California Department of Public Health urges people to get vaccinated and to monitor for symptoms of a fever coupled with an unexplained rash. They advise anyone who believes they’ve been infected to self-isolate and call a doctor immediately. State and local health officials are working to identify and notify anyone who may have been infected.

headlines.title: Multi-vehicle crash leaves six people injured in San Francisco
headlines.description: Six people were injured following a multi-vehicle crash in San Francisco Saturday, the fire department said. The fire department said the crash occurred in the area of Park Presidio and California streets just before 7 p.m. At the scene, firefighters declared a “yellow alert multi-casualty incident,” which authorities said brings more ambulances and secures adequate emergency room occupancy for trauma patients. The fire department said all six victims were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries; three of them have moderate injuries, while three have minor injuries. Authorities warned drivers to expected delays in the area of Park Presidio Boulevard and California Street.

headlines.title: Person with an axe arrested on Cupertino college campus
headlines.description: A person was arrested on the De Anza College campus in Cupertino, the De Anza Community College District Police Department said on Friday. Police said officers on patrol noticed a person acting suspiciously on campus and made contact. Authorities said a records check revealed the person had an outstanding felony warrant. Police said officers also found the suspect had an axe, suspected methamphetamine and heroin, loaded hypodermic needles and drug paraphernalia. The person was taken into custody and booked into the Santa Clara County Main Jail on multiple drug, weapons and warrant-related charges, according to authorities.

headlines.title: Man dies after crashing into building in Fremont
headlines.description: A man died after crashing into a building in Fremont on Saturday, according to the police department. Police said officers responded to a report of a single-vehicle crash at around 12:12 p.m. in the area of Niles Boulevard and Cinematic Common. At the scene, authorities said they found the unresponsive 88-year-old driver and provided life-saving efforts. The driver was taken to a local trauma center, where he later died, officials reported. Police said no bystanders were injured and the exact cause of the crash is under investigation, but “speed has not been ruled out”. Authorities added this is the city’s ninth fatal traffic collision in 2026.

headlines.title: UC Berkeley student says she was followed, chased into her apartment complex
headlines.description: A UC Berkeley student said she was followed and chased into her off-campus apartment building on Tuesday night. Berkeley junior Eden Winograd said this all happened at around 8 p.m. on Tuesday when she was walking her dog near her off-campus apartment complex. That night, Winograd said she was walking her dog on the same path she does every night when she noticed a man approaching whom she had seen a few days earlier. “I started to panic a little bit, but I didn’t want to offend him if he was just standing there,” she said, recalling that she then started crossing the street. But then, she said the man started following directly behind her and saying things to her while she walked. “I started speeding up and heard his feet banging on the floor behind me,” she said. “I went up to the gate, I buzzed myself in, I went, and I closed it, and then I heard clanging sounds while I was walking inside, and I turned around, and he was like scaling the gate,” Winograd continued. “My heart sank, I was out of breath, my heart was pounding,” she recalled. She made it inside the elevator of her building before anything else happened, then called the police. Winograd posted the surveillance video of the incident on TikTok, where it has now been viewed more than 858,000 times. That surveillance video has now also been shared by Berkeley Police. The video shows Winograd walking into the gate of her apartment complex, walking her dog on a leash. A few seconds later, a man can be seen climbing over the same gate where she entered and following in the same direction Winograd walked in, holding something in his hand. Police said that initial reports indicated the suspect had a knife in his hand, but investigators later found that the object was likely a barbecue lighter. It is still unclear why that man would be holding a barbecue lighter. But for Winograd, that doesn’t change how alarming this incident was. “I don’t care if they have a weapon in their hand or nothing in their hand, I don’t want to be chased the second I step out of my apartment. I don’t want to be chased and have to watch someone claw their way up a wall to get to where I live,” she said. Police said that the following day, they were called about the same man lying on the sidewalk in the same area. Berkeley police said they detained him and confirmed he was involved in “the prior trespassing incident.” Police did not arrest that man, but they did send a case to the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office for review. Police have not released the man’s name, but they said he is 50 years old and experiencing homelessness.

headlines.title: Disabled train prompts major BART delay
headlines.description: A disabled train between the Fremont and Union City stations caused delays on the Berryessa line on Saturday, according to BART. At 12:15 p.m., BART said a disabled train between the Fremont and Union City stations was major causing delays on the Berryessa line. Just before 2 p.m., BART announced that train was cleared out of the way and it was in the process of restoring normal service, adding there was still a 20-minute delay on the Berryessa line in the Richmond, Daly City and Berryessa directions. headlines.title: More possible victims of man posing as 49ers player come forward, FBI says
headlines.description: The FBI says the number of women who say they were tricked online by a man posing as a 49ers player has grown to 61. Investigators are working to verify that the newly identified women are, in fact, victims of Daejon Love and Taylor Chan. Love and Chan are charged with several crimes including wire fraud. The FBI says Love posed as a 49ers player on dating apps to meet women online. He would then ask them for money for fake investments while Chan posed as his financial adviser, according to authorities. The FBI is asking anyone with information about Love or Chan to contact the agency.

headlines.title: Surveillance video shows moment ICE agent's gun found in San Francisco airport bathroom
headlines.description: Surveillance video from San Francisco International Airport obtained by NBC Bay Area is shedding more light on a July incident where an ICE deportation officer allegedly left his gun unattended in an airport restroom. A review of roughly two hours of CCTV footage – obtained through a California Public Records Act request – shows the moment the gun was found inside a bathroom stall by a flight attendant, along with the likely moment the ICE agent returned to the scene roughly 10 minutes later. As NBC Bay Area first reported in August, the firearm was found unattended inside a bathroom stall past security checkpoint D in Terminal 2, according to airport spokesperson Doug Yakel. Around 10:23 p.m., the surveillance video shows a person who appears to be the flight attendant run out of the bathroom and flag down airport security. The flight attendant and security officer then head back to the bathroom. Airport security then calls 9-1-1 and reports the gun to San Francisco police. “Hi, yeah, a flight attendant just came up to me and said there is a gun in the men’s bathroom,” an airport security officer tells police in a recording of the 9-1-1 call. San Francisco Aug 26 San Francisco Aug 27 The video shows additional law enforcement officers quickly arrive to investigate. Multiple travelers are turned away from the bathroom by police or security. The video makes it clear that dozens of people could potentially have found the gun if the flight attendant had not spotted it and notified security. Roughly 10 minutes after the flight attendant appears to discover the gun, the surveillance video shows a man dressed in plain clothes approach security outside the bathroom, present what looks like a badge, and enter the bathroom. The airport confirmed the man seen in the video was the ICE agent returning for his firearm. The video shows the apparent ICE agent emerge from the bathroom more than 10 minutes later with other law enforcement officials. He remains in front of the bathroom, where he seems to talk to officers on scene and present some sort of identification. Officers soon verify the gun belongs to the agent, according to police radio traffic. “We verified his firearm serial number through the government website,” someone says in the recording. Due to the position of the video camera and the quality of the video, it was not immediately clear to NBC Bay Area when the agent may have first left the gun in the bathroom. For weeks, NBC Bay Area has been asking ICE if the agent has faced any discipline for misplacing his gun, but the agency has not responded.
headlines.source: Hilda Gutierrez, Michael Bott and Alex Bozovic
